children.text: A coastal town on the northern coast of Mindoro, reached from Manila by bus and boat in about
4–5 hours
. Facing the globally renowned Verde Island Passage, it is a popular entry point for diving, and White Beach and Sabang Beach let you combine beach relaxation with nightlife.

Puerto Galera is a coastal town at the northern tip of Mindoro island, across the sea from Batangas port. True to its name, "Port of the Galleons," it has been used since the Spanish era as a natural harbor for sheltering from storms, and its bay, ringed by islands and capes, is also listed as a member of the "Most Beautiful Bays in the World Club." In
it was designated a biosphere reserve under the UNESCO Man and the Biosphere (MAB) Programme.

Its biggest asset lies underwater. The Verde Island Passage between Luzon and Mindoro is so rich in coral and fish species that marine scientists call it "the center of the center of marine biodiversity," and Puerto Galera sits right at that strait's edge. Dozens of dive centers cluster around Sabang Beach, and coral gardens, canyons, wrecks, and macro-life sites lie just
5–20 minutes
away by boat, making it a long-familiar entry point for Korean divers too.

The beaches have distinct personalities. White Beach is a lively resort strip lined with restaurants and bars along a long stretch of sand, crowded with Filipino university students and families during summer break and Holy Week. Sabang Beach is a narrow beach centered on divers and nightlife, while Small La Laguna and Big La Laguna are quiet beaches next to Sabang with easy access for snorkeling and diving. The Talipanan Beach area to the west is much quieter.

Being close to Manila, it's a good place to leave on a Friday evening and spend the weekend. It especially suits people learning to dive, families and friends looking for a casual beach getaway, and Korean residents of the Philippines looking for the sea near Manila.
To gauge its scale, Puerto Galera is a municipality of Oriental Mindoro covering about 248 km² and made up of 13 barangays. As of the

census, its population is about 42,000. Tourists crowd only parts of the northern coastline, while the rest is mountains and forest, so another feature of the area is that a short drive from the beach leads to waterfalls and indigenous villages.
Dive centers in Sabang and La Laguna offer try-dives or a 3–4 day Open Water course. Some centers have Korean instructors, which eases the burden for beginners.

Popular sites include Canyons, where canyon terrain meets strong current; Hole in the Wall, which passes through a gap in the rock; and an artificial wreck site off Sabang. Sites with strong current should only be dived with an experienced buddy.
A popular half-day tour charters a bangka to visit the Coral Garden, a giant clam sanctuary, and small deserted beaches. It's best to leave in the morning when the water is clear.

blocks.title: Sunset and fire dancing at White Beach

children.text: At sunset, restaurants set their tables out on the sand along the beach, and fire-dance shows follow at night. It's a relaxed atmosphere families can enjoy comfortably too.
A waterfall along the coastal road to Calapan, about
30 minutes
by car from Puerto Galera town. There's a pool at the base, offering a different scene from the beaches.
You can visit an Iraya Mangyan community around Talipanan to buy traditional crafts and learn about their way of life. Always ask permission before taking photos.
The water in front of Small La Laguna is shallow enough to snorkel and kayak straight from the beach.
The wreck site off Sabang lies at a depth of
, so it is easy for beginners to reach, and the Alma Jane wreck is a cargo ship about
long standing upright on a sandy bottom at

, and the Canyons dive that follows is an intermediate-or-higher drift dive going down to around

From the Cubao and Buendia (Pasay) areas of Manila, air-conditioned buses of JAM Liner, JAC Liner, DLTB, ALPS, and others to Batangas port (including via the Batangas Grand Terminal) leave frequently from early morning until night. The first JAM Liner bus leaves Cubao at 1:00 AM, and the fare is around ₱207 from Cubao and ₱197 from Buendia. Depending on traffic it takes about
2 hours–3 hours 30 minutes
, and fares including other buses are about
. By Grab or a chartered van, you can get from your door to the port for about

From Batangas port to Balatero port in Puerto Galera, boats of Island Water, Galerian Water Transport, and Montenegro Lines make several trips from early morning until around 3–4 PM. Fast craft take about
1 hour–1 hour 30 minutes
and cost about
one-way, while RoRo ships take about
2 hours
and economy seats cost about
. Discounts are available for students, seniors, and persons with disabilities, and fuel surcharges can make the actual fare higher. The Batangas port terminal fee rose from

Most passenger ships come in at Balatero port, but the environmental fee is collected at six points: Balatero, Sabang, Muelle, and Minolo ports and the Villaflor and Aninuan overland boundaries. Sailing ports and fares change often, so check the latest notices from the shipping line and the municipal tourism office before you leave.

If you missed the boat to Balatero or arrive in Batangas late at night, you can take the Batangas–Calapan RoRo ship, which has far more sailings, to cross to Mindoro and continue overland. From Calapan port to Puerto Galera it is about
50km
by road, about
1 hour–1 hour 30 minutes
by shared van, and the fare is around
. You pass Tamaraw Falls on the way, so it is a good place for a short stop.

From Manila, take the SLEX and STAR Tollway to Batangas port. Only RoRo ships can carry vehicles, and loading one car costs about
depending on the shipping line, and a motorcycle about
. Tricycles are common locally, so many travelers leave the car near the port instead of taking it on board.
Before you leave, complete tourist registration on the PG-Pass website and get your QR code. You can pay the environmental fee online in advance when you register.
When you get off the bus, go straight to the ticket counter inside the port and buy your ticket. Avoid touts outside the port who offer private boats or marked-up tickets.
Pay the terminal fee, show your QR code at the gate, and board the boat.
When you land at Balatero port, show your registration code, and pay the environmental fee on the spot if you haven't yet.
Take a tricycle or van to the beach where your accommodation is.

A land tour of the waterfall, indigenous villages, and viewpoint costs about
per tricycle (for 3 people), and you should settle the route and fare before setting out.
November
to
May
is the dry season and the best time to travel. Especially from

to

, the sea is calm and visibility is good, making it the best diving season, and after April the water is warm at 28–32°C. However, White Beach gets very crowded and room rates rise sharply during Holy Week and the summer break (
March–May
), so we recommend visiting on weekdays or staying on the Sabang or Talipanan side during this period.
From
December
to
February
, the northeast monsoon Amihan brings wind and slightly cooler water, but the inner bay stays relatively sheltered, so diving is possible on many days. From
June
to
October

is the southwest monsoon Habagat and typhoon season, with frequent rain and days when the Batangas route is cancelled. Check the weather bureau's forecasts and coast guard sailing notices during this period.

Choose accommodation based on the purpose of your trip. For a beach getaway or family trip, the resorts and guesthouses of White Beach (about
per night) are convenient, with the beachfront restaurant strip right there. If diving is the goal, dive resorts in Sabang, where the dive centers are, or Small/Big La Laguna (about
per night) cut down on travel time. For a quiet rest, look for small resorts on the western Talipanan or Aninuan beaches. Be sure to book ahead for peak-season weekends and holidays.

The food centers on seafood barbecue along the beach restaurant strip. Walking White Beach in the evening, you'll find many restaurants displaying fish, shrimp, squid, and crab on ice, sold by weight and cooked however you like. Sabang Beach has many European-style restaurants and bars catering to divers, so pizza, pasta, and steak are easy to find too. For Filipino food, pork barbecue, sisig, and kinilaw (fish ceviche) are safe choices, and mango shakes are sold at nearly every restaurant. Expect beach restaurant prices to run 20–50% higher than in the cities.
To gauge the price range, as of May
, a simple room at White Beach is about
per night, a mid-range hotel about
, and a boutique resort about

. Sabang, popular with divers, has many long-established dive resorts, led by Captain Greg's, Asia Divers, and El Galleon Resort, which have operated since the early 1980s. Casa Mia Ristorante Italiano, at the western end of White Beach, is known as an Italian restaurant with a good beach view. At local eateries you can eat for
or less per meal, but restaurants right on the beach are much more expensive.
White Beach and Sabang have ATMs, but they often run out of cash or break down. It's best to withdraw plenty of cash in Batangas beforehand.
Batangas port is very crowded on Friday evenings and the day before a holiday, so it's best to take an early morning bus or book online through the shipping line if possible.
It's best to check a dive center's equipment condition, insurance coverage, and instructor qualifications before choosing. Prices that seem too cheap can mean overcrowded groups or faulty gear.
If you only plan to snorkel, the shallow water in front of Small La Laguna is enough without chartering a separate boat.
For island hopping offered by beach touts, it's best to fix the price and route before departure, and confirm whether coral garden entrance is included.
Sunset photos come out well from the western end of White Beach or facing Talipanan, capturing the sun setting over the sea.
Phone signal is good at most beaches, but can be weak at some resorts deep in the bay.
Tourists entering Puerto Galera can pass quickly through Balatero port if they register in advance on the electronic entry registration system
PG-Pass
and get a QR code. The environmental fee is about
per person, and students, seniors, and persons with disabilities get a 20% discount by showing ID. Register on the
official PG-Pass website
If you take a Montenegro Lines ship, from
March 2026

online pre-registration with ORAS is mandatory at Batangas port under Philippine Ports Authority (PPA) guidelines, so register in advance and get your QR code. Passengers who bought tickets online and passengers traveling with vehicles are exempt.
The standard for island hopping is about
per boat (6–8 people). For some sites, such as the giant clam sanctuary, the cost of transferring to a smaller boat is charged separately at about
per person, and the area around the underwater cave is rocky, so aqua shoes come in handy.
You must not fly within
24 hours
of diving, so if you have a return flight, be sure to calculate your last dive date accordingly.
Sites with strong current like Canyons are dangerous for beginners, so choose sites that match your experience level.
Don't step on or touch coral at the beach, and be careful with fin kicks in protected areas.
Some nightlife venues at Sabang Beach can involve touting and overcharging, so confirm prices before ordering.
During the rainy and typhoon season, ferries can be cancelled without notice, so it's best to leave buffer time in your return schedule.
Jellyfish appear at certain times of year, so wear a rash guard, and rinse with vinegar if stung.
Pay for and buy environmental fees and tickets only at the port's official counters or on the PG-Pass website. Tickets and private boats sold by touts are sometimes overpriced.

A vast coral reef nature park west of Mindoro; reachable from Puerto Galera by land and boat in nearly a day, but a good continuation for a diving trip.
An active volcano on an island within the lake, a good stop on the way to or from Batangas.
A small volcanic island in the middle of the Verde Island Passage, famous for wall diving. It takes about
30–45 minutes
